Run scATAC quality control metrics

Source: R/RunATACQC.R
RunATACQC.Rd

Calculate common scATAC QC metrics and optionally filter cells by thresholds.

Usage

RunATACQC(
  object,
  assay = NULL,
  tss.positions = NULL,
  blacklist = NULL,
  fast = TRUE,
  min_pct_reads_in_peaks = NULL,
  min_TSS_enrichment = NULL,
  max_nucleosome_signal = NULL,
  max_blacklist_ratio = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE,
  srt = NULL,
  frip.columns = NULL,
  frip = FALSE,
  frip.chunk.size = 100000L
)

Arguments

object

A Seurat object.

assay

Assay to use. NULL uses the default assay.

tss.positions

TSS positions passed to Signac::TSSEnrichment. An explicit value requests recalculation, even when an imported TSS score exists.

blacklist

A GRanges blacklist used to compute blacklist_ratio.

fast

Whether to use the fast mode in Signac::TSSEnrichment.

min_pct_reads_in_peaks, min_TSS_enrichment, max_nucleosome_signal, max_blacklist_ratio

Optional thresholds used for filtering cells. Fraction thresholds use 0–1, not percentages. A requested metric must be present and finite for every cell; missing or failed calculations never silently disable a requested filter.

verbose

Whether to print the message. Default is TRUE.

srt

Deprecated alias for object; supply exactly one of the two. It will be removed in scop 1.0.0.

frip.columns

Optional named character vector with in_peaks and total metadata column names. Supplying these explicitly asserts that both count the same read/fragment unit over the same files, cells and filtering rules, and that the numerator refers to the current peak universe. Legacy column names are not guessed. Without either this argument or frip = TRUE, an existing pct_reads_in_peaks column is preserved, but a new FRiP is not inferred from matrix column sums.

frip

Explicitly recalculate a fragment-record fraction overlapping the current peak union. Each record counts once, even across several peaks. Duplicate input rows remain separate records; column-five support is not used as a weight. Stores frip and the legacy 0–1 alias.

frip.chunk.size

Maximum fragment records read per sequential block.

Value

A Seurat object, retaining input cell order or the ordered subset passing all requested thresholds. Available metadata include fragment counts, nucleosome_signal, nucleosome_percentile, TSS.enrichment, pct_reads_in_peaks and blacklist_ratio. Direct fragment FRiP also writes frip and a scop_frip receipt in the assay's misc slot, recording the peak union, mapped cells, source hashes and per-cell numerator/denominator. Explicit source-column recalculation also synchronizes frip and clears any previous direct-fragment receipt. Metrics are calculated only for cells in the selected assay; other cells and their existing metadata are preserved. Filtering removes only failed cells from the selected assay; at least one cell in that assay must pass the requested thresholds. Zero denominators produce NA; requested filters reject unavailable or non-finite metrics. Fraction metrics use 0–1, not percentages.

Details

total.fragments counts fragment-file records (frequency_count), not column-five read support (reads_count). Each file's explicit Signac barcode mapping is applied separately, so captures may reuse the same raw barcode. Resources without selected-assay cells are ignored during calculation but remain attached to the returned assay. blacklist_ratio is the fraction of peak-matrix counts assigned to peaks overlapping any blacklist interval. Each peak contributes once; it is not a fragment-level blacklist fraction. Existing QC columns are imported values; callers must verify their source, units and relevance after changing peaks. Explicit FRiP source columns must not use names overwritten by fragment counting (frequency_count, reads_count, mononucleosomal, nucleosome_free, total.fragments); retain upstream values under distinct names when attaching fragments. TSS enrichment uses Signac's R implementation and does not select an external backend merely because a newer Signac release exports it. Missing optional inputs leave metrics unavailable. This function does not perform doublet detection or establish that all fragment QC is complete.

See also

ReadATACData(), CheckATACData()

Examples

counts <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(
  i = c(1, 2, 1, 2), j = c(1, 1, 2, 2), x = c(2, 1, 1, 3),
  dimnames = list(c("chr1-1-10", "chr1-21-30"), c("cell1", "cell2"))
)
ranges <- GenomicRanges::makeGRangesFromDataFrame(data.frame(
  seqnames = "chr1", start = c(1L, 21L), end = c(10L, 30L)
))
object <- ReadATACData(counts, ranges = ranges, genome = "toy", verbose = FALSE)
object$source_in_peaks <- c(3, 4)
object$source_total <- c(5, 8)
object <- RunATACQC(object,
  frip.columns = c(in_peaks = "source_in_peaks", total = "source_total"),
  min_pct_reads_in_peaks = 0.5, verbose = FALSE
)
object$pct_reads_in_peaks
#> cell1 cell2 
#>   0.6   0.5
